title: Tool schema orchestration and precise error mapping
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a lightweight orchestration layer for tool/function JSON schemas that enables runtime adaptation between schema versions, typed parameter profiles, and human-friendly error mapping. Deliverables: a canonical schema wrapper, a runtime adaptor that can coerce legacy payloads into the canonical form with safety checks, a compact error code taxonomy with remediation hints, and an integration test harness. This work targets both the hosted API and the Dedicated/Private runtime agent so SDKs and internal routing can surface consistent errors and migration guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical schema wrapper defined and documented (less than 3 pages) with examples for optional/required/union/array/enum cases
Runtime adaptor implemented in the serving runtime that performs non-destructive coercion modes (strict, best-effort, repair) behind a feature flag
Error code taxonomy (E-TC-000 to E-TC-099) published with user-facing messages and internal debug payloads
End-to-end tests cover: exact-match schema, minor-compat coercions, and recoverable failures with suggested fixes
SDKs receive a compatibility shim that maps legacy tool manifests to canonical fields without new API surface
implementation_notes: Introduce a small canonical envelope: {name, version, params, param_profiles} (documented in Confluence); runtime reads envelope and selects validator
Support three validation modes: strict (reject), permissive-coerce (coerce trivial type mismatches), repair-suggest (return structured error with patch suggestion)
Leverage existing schema test corpus from ENG-615233 and extend with 120 synthetic edge cases (nested unions, long arrays, missing defaults)
Keep runtime fallback path small: if adaptor cannot coerce, return mapped error code and include minimal example payload in debug logs only (never leak customer data)
Quantize error messages to a short title + remediation hint + link to docs; avoid free-form error text in production responses

testing_plan: Unit tests for each validation mode with positive and negative cases
Fuzz test harness to generate malformed params and assert deterministic error codes
Integration tests: host->runtime->sdk roundtrip using canary feature flag
Load test to verify that permissive-coerce path does not increase median p50 latency by >5%
Manual QA checklist for UX of error messages in Console and SDKs
rollout_notes: Phase 1: Deploy adaptor to staging behind feature flag. Run compatibility sweep against production manifests in read-only mode
Phase 2: Enable permissive-coerce for 5% of traffic for non-critical customers; monitor error-rate, latency, and repair-success ratio
Phase 3: Expand to 100% for hosted API once repair-suggest path is available and docs are published
Dedicated/Private: Ship as opt-in runtime bundle; provide migration guide and toggle in Console
